_comment: OpenShift releases this plugin is built for, one image per entry. This file is the single
source of truth: the CI, release and rebuild matrices are generated from it, and
scripts/sync-targets.mjs writes each entry into targets/<minor>/.
A single bundle cannot span releases. The console supplies react, react-router and
react-i18next as shared singletons via module federation, and those versions change between
releases - most sharply at 4.22, where the console moved React 17 -> 18. A plugin built
against the wrong set loads and then fails silently: the pod serves assets, the console skips
the plugin, and every route 404s with nothing in any server-side log.
The repo is split along that axis. Build tooling - webpack, eslint, jest, typescript - is
target-independent and lives in the root package.json under one Dependabot-maintained
lockfile. Everything that ends up in the bundle, or that ConsoleRemotePlugin reads from the
process cwd, gets a directory each under targets/ with its own lockfile, so every shipped
image is built from a reviewed, pinned tree under `yarn install --immutable`.
Yarn 4 removed the `lockfileFilename` setting, so per-target lockfiles cannot sit side by side
at the repo root - a directory each is the only layout Yarn 4 supports, and also the only one
Dependabot can maintain, because it keys npm updates on a directory. Every target needs its
own npm entry in .github/dependabot.yml; src/ocp-targets.spec.ts fails if one is missing.
Field by field:
'sdk'          the SDK line whose validator enforces that release's contract.
'shared'       the module-federation singletons the console provides. ConsoleRemotePlugin
derives the bundle's shared set from the target's DECLARED dependencies, not
from what the source imports, so a stale entry here changes what the plugin
asks the console to share.
'pins'         bundled devDependencies that track the target's React major.
'routerModule' the package src/compat re-exports from. react-router 5.3 exports neither Link
nor useSearchParams, so the React 17 releases take them from
react-router-dom-v5-compat, which those consoles share and 4.22 does not.
'bundled'      (top level) deps every target needs but whose versions Dependabot owns per
directory. Used only to seed a new target directory.
To add a target: add an entry, run `node scripts/sync-targets.mjs`, add an npm entry to
.github/dependabot.yml, then install and build it:
cd targets/<minor> && yarn install && OCP_TARGET=<minor> yarn --cwd ../.. build
A mismatch is reported as 'Console provides shared module X but plugin uses Y'.
4.23 is not built yet: its SDK is still 4.23.0-prerelease.5, so the shared-module contract can
still change before GA.
